<a id="book-model"></a>

# Book Model

A book has a fixed hierarchy: a book root with a title, chapters, and one level of subchapters. Link entries are siblings of chapters and point to another location, local or in another book.

The fixed depth keeps output predictable. A subchapter cannot contain another subchapter; the core rejects it with a stable error instead of inventing another level.

Bodies are blocks. A node holds an ordered list of blocks; a paragraph, a code sample or a note is one block. The block is the only body in the model, so there is no second place where text can live.

Every block has an identifier, an optional type, an optional lock and an optional status. The text itself lives in the body store, not in the manifest. Locked blocks belong to the tool and reject manual body changes.

Regions hold content outside the node flow: the book footer, one notes region per target, and one index-prose block per node. A region has a target, an ordered block list and its own identifier.

The manifest is version 5. It holds the tree, the regions, block metadata, the status configuration, the declared badges, the repository-layout configuration and the book settings, including the optional book language and the optional README layout. It never holds a body.

Identifiers are stable and never reused. Moving a node or a block keeps its identifier; a copy receives a new one. The library ledger hands out every identifier, so uniqueness is a constraint rather than a probability.

Open and close are the storage state. Open extracts the container into the store for editing; close packs it again. Authoring commands require an open book, while sync, check and verify read either state.

Validation runs on every mutation and on close. It checks the tree, placement, body presence, the prose rule, status assignments, the layout configuration, badges and identifiers, and it reports all issues in one pass.

Persisted formats carry explicit versions. A book written by an older release is still read, but any manifest or body write refuses with `migrate.required` until `pecia migrate apply --book <id> --write` upgrades it; `book open` and `book close` stay available, and close preserves the source manifest version.
